bar.name: v1 HTML fixtures and A2UI for the same apps; 300 blind English requests; independent end-to-end attack on stored rows

biggest_gap: Restoring a backup copies the backup's clock into the running app, so new rows are dated the backup's day and 'today' is wrong; load with data ignores `now`. Safe edits also reset state declared inside an `each` block (per-option counters, open rows).

acceptance.line: >= 90% of 300 blind requests expressible (programs parse and type-check)
acceptance.evidence: mo.mjs check: 330 of 330 OK. Coverage of unseen requests not re-measured.
300 corpus programs: keyword tokenizer median 133, p90 239, max 811.

acceptance.line: every prefix cut at a line end parses
acceptance.evidence: Prefix test passes inside 556/556; fuzz-check 20,000 mutations on a fresh seed: 0 crashes, 0 grammar mismatches.

acceptance.line: edits never lose or retype saved data while marked safe
acceptance.evidence: Rows, settings and picks survived 124k critic steps on 31 programs plus about 600 edits over 330 programs. But a safe edit resets block-scoped state: an option rename or a heading added above an `each` turns a tasbeeh count of 3 into 8 (3 of 330 programs).

other_notes: S2: setField on the built-in `at` field accepts empty and out-of-range values, wiping the row's time so it leaves every date window.

S3 but must fix for real use: at 2,000 rows a tap takes 1.3 s on the budget example and tick(1 day) with an `every 1s` rule takes 55 s; each Undo step stores a whole-data JSON (about 20 MB at 50 steps).
All nine round 8 faults confirmed fixed. Date windows, streaks, timers across reload and midnight, two forms, 50-step undo, emoji/RTL round trips all passed by hand.
